description: Beyond the explicit child history content, the flow may implicitly disclose extra personal data through metadata such as timing, frequency, routing, object names, or attachment characteristics.

title: Parent can link child history with other family members' data
description: Once received, the parent user may combine the child's history with other household or sibling information already available to them, enabling broader linkage across individuals.
uncertainty_note: This depends on what other data the parent has and whether such combination creates a privacy-relevant threat in the intended context.

title: Received history contains revealing attributes that identify the child
description: The child history received by the parent may contain attributes such as age, events, dates, conditions, or contextual details that make the child readily identifiable.

title: Received child history can serve as attributable evidence about the child
description: The history data itself may be used by the recipient as evidence to attribute past actions, events, or statuses to the child, reducing deniability.

title: Child may be unaware that their history is disclosed to the parent
description: At the destination, the parent receives and can review the child's history, while the child as data subject may not be aware that this disclosure and review is taking place.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not state the child's age, notice mechanisms, or whether such parental access is expected and communicated.

title: Child may lack access to what history was shared with the parent
description: The data subject may have limited ability to see exactly what child history was disclosed to the parent, reducing transparency and control over the processing.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible downstream control issue, but the flow alone does not confirm whether the child has access rights or visibility.

title: Disclosure to parent may lack an appropriate lawful basis or proper authorization
description: If the parent is not entitled to receive the specific child history, or if the disclosure conditions are not legally valid for the child's context, the receipt and processing at the destination may be unlawful.
uncertainty_note: The flow alone does not establish the governing legal basis, parental authority scope, or jurisdiction-specific rules.

title: Source may violate data minimization when returning child history
description: If P3 returns more child-history data than necessary for parent review, the source processing may violate the data minimization principle.

title: Source may disclose records retained beyond necessity
description: If P3 includes historical records that should no longer be retained or used for this purpose, the source processing may violate storage limitation requirements.
uncertainty_note: Retention obligations are not specified; this threat depends on whether obsolete records are actually included.
